answer.rationale: Competitor price cut has doubled churn conversations in price-sensitive SMB segment. Memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective for this cohort with strong acquisition and revenue lift. However, this is a defensive move with real downstream risk: promotional pricing can erode willingness-to-pay and long-term unit economics if not bounded. Strategy: deploy promotional pricing as a time-limited, segment-specific response (SMB accounts at churn risk) rather than broad pricing change. Simultaneously activate memory_31 (simplified signup) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding) to reinforce stickiness and reduce price sensitivity over time by improving value realization speed. Reference memory_57 shows referral incentives work but are concentrated in mature accounts, not ideal for acute SMB churn. Memory_44 reminds that enterprise pipeline quality matters; protect sales-assist capacity for higher-LTV prospects. Standard experiment scale allows measured rollout to at-risk SMB cohort while monitoring for negative elasticity signals. Preserve uncertainty: promotional response is necessary but carries retention/margin risk if extended beyond immediate competitive threat window.
